item.title: R&B
item.description: On November 18, 1954, in an Atlanta radio studio, Ray Charles recorded “I Got a Woman” by pouring secular words into a gospel tune, and the collision of church voice and dance-floor rhythm became the engine of Black popular music for the rest of the century.

item.title: Soul
item.description: Crooner-style horns enter first on “Try a Little Tenderness”: no drums yet, no rhythm section punching at the listener, just Otis Redding’s restrained vocal moving softly over Duck Dunn’s bass.
